brief: USTs extend Friday's selloff, led by the long end. The 10Y yield breaks 4.75% and September hike pricing rises to about 70%. Mizuho's US economist argues that since Warsh's Jackson Hole appearance, the burden of proof has shifted from why hike to why not hike, so soft data must now stop the Fed rather than firm data pushing it further. Oil reinforces the hold case. US strikes on Iranian launchers preceded Iranian retaliation against US bases, and Brent above $90 keeps the inflation channel open. JOLTS and ISM print today, with Mizuho forecasting upside surprises (7.62mn, 55.8) that would reinforce Fed-hold pressure. Friday's NFP is the week's key event, where Mizuho sees downside risk (30k) against the Street's 58k. Bunds sell off despite softer German inflation as energy and September supply dominate. Today's EZ print matters more for core and services than the headline. Gilts reopen into a worse backdrop, facing a mechanical bearish catch-up, compounded by UK shop-price inflation at a two-year high that Mizuho does not expect to settle the BoE debate. JGB yields rise on the global selloff and a weak auction, and USDJPY climbs toward 160.
